newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish central bank sells dlrs for lira - bankers.
newsitem.headline: Turkish central bank sells dlrs for lira - bankers.

text.p: Turkey's central bank began selling dollars for lira to banks in afternoon trade on Thursday, to curb the U.S. currency's rise buoyed by excess lira liquidity in the money market, bankers said.
The lira firmed to 108,200 against the dollar from around 108,300 before the intervention.
Bankers said the central bank checked dollar bid rates of a few banks earlier in the afternoon, causing the lira to firm to 108,300 to the dollar from a low of 108,560 it touched in the morning.
"The central bank sold dollars for lira to a few banks in early afternoon just to check the rates. It intervened more heavily towards the close," said a private banker.
The money market opened with a 150.9 trillion lira surplus due to maturing inflation-indexed state securities used by banks to meet their liquidity requirements.
The central bank drained 57.1 trillion lira via a three-month reverse repo auction on the open market in the morning which left about 94 trillion lira idle in the market.
Overnight money traded mostly at around 65 percent, up from 57.62 percent average on Tuesday when trade was thin due to half-day work in financial markets ahead of the new year holiday.
